hypotheses: A category and a presheaf morphism F→G.
conclusions: A unique subpresheaf G' of G receives a surjection from F and factors the original morphism.

hypotheses: A functor u:C→D preserving existing fibre products and equalizers in C.
conclusions: For every V in D, the opposite of the category I_V satisfies the two conditions on common-source arrow comparison and parallel-arrow equalization from the pinned Categories lemma.
lemma-almost-directed.review_note: Need replace cited lemma with both exact quantified conditions; no nonemptiness asserted.

hypotheses: A functor u:C→D preserving fibre products, with a final object X in C whose image is final in D.
conclusions: Each opposite indexing category I_V^opp is filtered (nonempty, admits cocones for pairs of objects, and coequalizes parallel arrows).
lemma-directed.review_note: Definition-directed is terminology, not another hypothesis.

hypotheses: A functor u:C→D and its source-defined functors u_p and u^p on presheaves.
conclusions: u_p is left adjoint to u^p, naturally in the two presheaf arguments.

hypotheses: A functor u:C→D and an object U of C.
conclusions: u_p h_U is canonically isomorphic to h_{u(U)}.

hypotheses: Two families of morphisms with the same fixed target in a category.
conclusions: Combinatorial equivalence implies tautological equivalence; tautological equivalence implies mutual refinement; each of these three relations is an equivalence relation.

hypotheses: Two same-target families, with stated fibre products existing, which are tautologically equivalent.
conclusions: A presheaf obeys the sheaf condition for one family if and only if it obeys the sheaf condition for the other.

hypotheses: A same-target morphism V→U of families specified by identity, index map and component maps; F(U)→product F(V_j) injective.
conclusions: F(U)→product F(U_i) is injective.

hypotheses: A same-target morphism of families, existence of listed fibre products, sheaf condition for V, and injectivity of all specified maps on each U_i.
conclusions: The sheaf condition holds for U.

hypotheses: Two sets of coverings each defining a site on the same category.
conclusions: Under one-way tautological-equivalence coverage, sheaves for Cov_2 are included in sheaves for Cov_1; symmetric coverage gives equality.
Under one-way refinement coverage, the same inclusion holds; symmetric refinement coverage gives equality.

hypotheses: A proper class of coverings obeying all three site axioms, with two subsets defining sites and each containing a combinatorially equivalent representative of every class covering.
conclusions: The two resulting sheaf categories are equal.
lemma-choice-set-coverings-immaterial.review_note: Expand cited Definition of site to explicit axioms, not additional premises.

hypotheses: A group G and its site T_G satisfying the source-specified properties; the functors F↦F(G) and S↦F_S.
conclusions: The evaluation and functor-of-points constructions give quasi-inverse equivalences between sheaves on T_G and G-Sets.

hypotheses: A site C and a diagram I→Sh(C).
conclusions: The diagram has a limit in Sh(C), computed by the same presheaf limit.

hypotheses: A site C, a presheaf F and its source-defined covering-colimit plus construction.
conclusions: The plus construction forms a presheaf and yields a canonical morphism F→F^+.

hypotheses: A site C and the plus construction on its presheaves.
conclusions: The map sending F to (F→F^+) is functorial in F.

hypotheses: Two coverings of the same U in a site C.
conclusions: There exists a covering of U refining both.

hypotheses: Two morphisms of coverings f,g:U→V with the same target map, and a presheaf F.
conclusions: They induce identical maps H0(V,F)→H0(U,F).

hypotheses: A presheaf F on a site C, object U, and section s∈F^+(U).
conclusions: There exists a covering of U over which s is locally in the image of F→F^+.

hypotheses: A presheaf F and a sheaf G on a site, with a morphism F→G.
conclusions: The morphism factors uniquely through the canonical map F→F# to a morphism F#→G.

hypotheses: A diagram of sheaves on a site.
conclusions: Its colimit in sheaves exists and is sheafification of its colimit in presheaves.

hypotheses: The sheafification functor PSh(C)→Sh(C) on a site C.
conclusions: The sheafification functor is exact.

hypotheses: A site C, presheaf F, object U and section of F# on U.
conclusions: A covering of U and local lifts of the section exist, agreeing after suitable further coverings of overlaps.
Conversely locally compatible sections determine a unique global sheafified section with the prescribed local images.

hypotheses: A map F→G of presheaves on a site, locally bijective on a covering of every object.
conclusions: The induced map F#→G# is an isomorphism.
